correctness.rationale: The definition forces the smallest prime to be \(2\) and the Egyptian-fraction value to be exactly \(1\). Reducing the exact identity modulo each maximal prime power gives \(m(1+s+\cdots+s^{a-1})\equiv1\pmod{s^a}\). The squarefree branch and all three exponent partitions of total multiplicity four are exhausted. Each survivor is checked by an exact reciprocal identity. A finite scan through \(200000\) was used only as regression evidence, not as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest broader-looking result classifies exactly two distinct prime divisors, so it has disjoint support size and cannot imply a three-support theorem. Machacek gives sufficient constructions and explicitly notes that the main sufficient condition is not necessary; those statements do not exhaust the low-multiplicity three-support cases.
